items.title: Average salary of €2,000 needed to buy a home in Spain
items.body: A net monthly salary of €1,999 is needed on average to buy a home in Spain without over-indebtedness, according to a study by Accumin Intelligence. In San Sebastian, buyers require €5,074; in Barcelona and Madrid, more than €4,000. Zamora is the cheapest provincial capital at €1,279.

items.title: Euribor rises above 2.8%; economist urges mortgage switch
items.body: The 12-month Euribor has risen above 2.8% in June, with a daily rate of 2.929%. This could increase variable mortgage payments by up to €133 per month. Economist Gonzalo Bernardos recommends switching to fixed-rate or capped mortgages to secure lower payments.

items.title: Eurozone inflation rises to 3.2% in May
items.body: Eurozone annual inflation accelerated to 3.2% in May, up from 3.0% in April, driven by a 10.8% rise in energy prices. Core inflation, excluding energy and food, stood at 2.6%. The increase raises living costs for households across the eurozone.

items.title: Inditex agrees 12.5% wage increase for store employees
items.body: Inditex has agreed with unions on a 12.5% salary increase until 2028 for nearly 30,000 store employees in Spain. The deal includes 4% annual raises in 2026, 2027, and 2028. Sunday pay rises to €11.25 per hour and holiday pay to €13.50 by 2028. Birth aid increases from €450 to €506.

items.title: Council of Europe urges Spain to reform unfair dismissal law
items.body: The Council of Europe has reiterated that Spain's unfair dismissal compensation of 33 days per year violates the European Social Charter. It calls for reforms to make compensation cover actual damages and be dissuasive. The Spanish government is urged to amend the legislation, which could strengthen job security for all workers.

items.title: European Parliament approves toughest EU immigration rules
items.body: The European Parliament has approved what it calls the toughest immigration regulations in EU history. Last year, over 719,000 irregular immigrants were identified in the EU, but only just over a quarter of the 491,000 expulsion orders were executed. In Spain, just 5,705 of 53,700 orders were enforced.

items.title: Fed chair keeps rates unchanged at 3.5%-3.75%
items.body: Kevin Warsh, the new Federal Reserve chair, kept U.S. interest rates unchanged at 3.5% to 3.75% in his first meeting, citing rising inflation. The decision was unanimous. Oil prices fell after an initial agreement between the US and Iran.

items.title: Magnific (Freepik) cuts 30% of Spanish staff in restructuring
items.body: Magnific, formerly Freepik, has started an ERE layoff process affecting 30% of its Spanish workforce, around 100 employees. The company, with 350 staff in Spain and €196 million annual recurring revenue, is restructuring to focus on AI, not due to financial issues.

items.title: Catalan doctors hold 12th strike, threaten escalation
items.body: Doctors in Catalonia held their 12th strike day before summer, demanding better conditions. The Metges de Catalunya union threatens to escalate the conflict in September if the government fails to negotiate. The government reported 4.2% strike participation; the union says 29%.

items.title: Intense heatwave expected in Spain from Sunday
items.body: Spain's state weather agency AEMET has warned of an intense and persistent heatwave starting Sunday June 21. Temperatures could exceed 36-38°C inland, reaching 40°C in eastern areas and up to 42°C locally. Monday June 22 is expected to be the peak day.

items.title: Chinese automaker Changan sets up European HQ in Madrid
items.body: Chinese automaker Changan has established its European headquarters in Alcobendas, Madrid. The company aims to sell 300,000 vehicles in Europe within three years and is evaluating the construction of a manufacturing plant in Aragon.

items.title: Wildfire burned area in Spain triples so far in 2026
items.body: From January to June 2026, 39,296 hectares have burned in Spain, three times more than the same period in 2025 (12,625 hectares). There have been 254 wildfires, up from 76, with eight large fires recorded, double the average.
